phase_1.summary: Phase 1 successfully sets up a React + Vite + Tailwind CSS application using Yjs for a local-first Kanban board persisted via y-indexeddb. By using statically defined top-level Y.Arrays for column sequencing (col-todo, col-in-progress, col-done) instead of dynamic nested maps, we eliminated LWW overwrite vulnerability YJS-01. The UI uses native HTML5 Drag & Drop and supports full creation, editing, deletion, and movement of cards, routing all state modifications cleanly through Yjs transactions with robust validation (title, description, assignee length limits) and defensive checks against orphaned references.
phase_1.done_criteria: with the browser's network tab fully disabled, every interaction (create/edit/delete cards, drag cards) works correctly and persists across a page reload using y-indexeddb and Yjs API.

phase_2.summary: Phase 2 successfully implements real-time online synchronization by integrating a Node.js y-websocket server (server.js) with client-side WebsocketProviders. The server enforces a strict per-board access control policy during WebSocket upgrades, checking the boardId and authorization token parameters defensively against a secure registry initialized with Object.create(null) to mitigate prototype pollution crashes (SEC-01). Client-side WebSocket URL query parameters are encoded using encodeURIComponent to prevent URL parameter injection (SEC-02). Real-time syncing, connection state updates, dynamic document switching, and board data isolation have been fully tested and verified by QA with 20 passing unit/integration tests.
phase_2.done_criteria: a card move/edit in one tab appears in the other tab within normal sync latency using y-websocket/Hocuspocus provider, no manual refresh.

phase_3.summary: Phase 3 successfully verifies offline-online transition and deterministic conflict merge semantics. An automated test script (tests/divergent_merge.js) was created to simulate client disconnection via provider.disconnect(), apply conflicting movements of a card X to different columns concurrently on Client A and Client B, and reconnect them via provider.connect(). Over 5 iterations, both clients consistently and deterministically converged to the exact same merged state. This outcome is documented in detail inside MERGE_SEMANTICS.md, explaining how Yjs's underlying CRDT structures resolve concurrent Y.Array additions (resulting in the card being present in both columns) without losing edits or card definitions.
phase_3.done_criteria: divergent offline merge scenario run at least 5 times with consistent, documented, no-data-loss outcomes, and MERGE_SEMANTICS.md explaining it in plain language.

phase_4.summary: Phase 4 successfully integrates user presence and offline status visibility. Collaborators can view and customize their names, which are broadcasted securely to other peers with strict input validation to mitigate DoS (SEC-03). The client monitors connection status via WebsocketProvider events, correctly counting and showing pending local updates generated while offline, and automatically resets the pending changes count to 0 upon reconnection. QA has validated all presence, connection status, and offline buffer reset operations, completing the final phase of the syncstack project with 25 passing test suites.
phase_4.done_criteria: awareness presence active; UI indicator shows synced vs offline, N pending local changes; disconnecting mid-session shows pending-changes accurately, clearing on sync.
